members.name: flag
members.summary: True when a --flag (or its short form) is present in argv.

members.name: value
members.summary: The value of a --name option as an Option.

members.name: fromBase64
members.summary: Decode standard base64 (padded or unpadded) to Bytes; raises on malformed input. The binary door Str.fromBase64 deliberately is not.

members.name: length
members.summary: The byte count as a Size.

members.name: sha256
members.summary: The SHA-256 digest of the bytes, lowercase hex (sha256sum parity).

members.name: toBase64
members.summary: Base64 of the bytes — ONE unwrapped line; the deliberate text exit (print and the boundaries refuse raw bytes).

members.name: tryFromBase64
members.summary: fromBase64 as an Option: None for malformed base64.

members.name: copy
members.summary: Copy a directory and its contents — (src, dst); refuses an existing destination (Dir.deleteAll first to replace). Copying a directory MEANS its contents: there is no non-recursive form.
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
Dir.copy d $"{d}-c"
Dir.deleteAll d
Dir.deleteAll $"{d}-c"

members.name: create
members.summary: Create a directory AND its parents; succeeds silently when it already exists (idempotent — an existing directory IS the post-condition; the one deliberate exception to refuse-overwrite).

members.name: delete
members.summary: Delete an EMPTY directory (refuses a non-empty one, naming Dir.deleteAll; raises when absent).

members.name: deleteAll
members.summary: DELETE THE DIRECTORY AND EVERYTHING UNDER IT, recursively. The destructive one — there is no undo.

members.name: exists
members.summary: True when the directory exists.

members.name: list
members.summary: The directory's entries as FULL paths — files and directories both, SORTED (the glob precedent), eager. Filter with Seq.where + File.exists/Dir.exists; `Path.glob "**"` is the recursive spelling.

members.name: move
members.summary: Move (rename) a directory — (src, dst); refuses an existing destination.

members.name: stat
members.summary: The directory's entries as ROWS — Dir.list's seq<FileRow> form, ls's own rows over the named directory (ls reads the cwd; Dir.stat reads elsewhere). Sorted by name, eager.

members.name: average
members.summary: The mean duration, truncated to whole milliseconds (raises on empty).

members.name: h
members.summary: A duration of n hours.

members.name: m
members.summary: A duration of n minutes.

members.name: ms
members.summary: A duration of n milliseconds — the literal 500ms, as a function.

members.name: parse
members.summary: Parse duration text — the shape show renders: 1h30m, 2.5s, 500ms (raises on anything else, including sub-millisecond precision).

members.name: s
members.summary: A duration of n seconds.

members.name: sleep
members.summary: Block for the duration (zero returns immediately; a negative duration raises; OS timer granularity applies — ~15ms Windows, ~1ms Linux — so a small sleep is a floor, not a promise). Module-qualified on purpose: bare sleep stays the coreutils command.

members.name: sum
members.summary: Sum durations.

members.name: toMillis
members.summary: The total milliseconds as an int (ratios, JSON fields).

members.name: toSeconds
members.summary: The total seconds as a float, lossless (2500ms is 2.5).

members.name: tryParse
members.summary: Duration.parse as an Option — None instead of the raise.

members.name: fromFile
members.summary: Read `.env` lines (KEY=value) as EnvVar records.

members.name: get
members.summary: A process environment variable as an Option.

members.name: ofPairs
members.summary: Build EnvVar records from name/value tuples.

members.name: pair
members.summary: Build one EnvVar from a name and value.

members.name: vars
members.summary: Every environment variable as EnvVar records.

members.name: append
members.summary: Append a sequence of lines to a file.

members.name: copy
members.summary: Copy src to dst — (src, dst), the universal convention (neither arg is 'the data', so data-last does not apply). REFUSES an existing destination (raises naming it); delete first to overwrite.
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
["x"] |> File.write $"{d}/a.txt"
File.copy $"{d}/a.txt" $"{d}/b.txt"
Dir.deleteAll d

members.name: delete
members.summary: Delete a file (raises naming the path when absent). The explicit pre-step for an overwriting copy/move.
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
["x"] |> File.write $"{d}/f.txt"
File.delete $"{d}/f.txt"
Dir.delete d

members.name: exists
members.summary: True when a path exists.

members.name: mode
members.summary: The path's permissions as rwxr-xr-x-shaped text, an Option — None on Windows (the platform limit stated, never invented). The READ follows a symlink (the File.* rule); existence does not — a dangling link raises naming the dangle. The receipt: the 0600 check before File.readSecret is File.mode p == Some "rw-------".

members.name: move
members.summary: Move (rename) src to dst — (src, dst); refuses an existing destination.
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
["x"] |> File.write $"{d}/a.txt"
File.move $"{d}/a.txt" $"{d}/b.txt"
Dir.deleteAll d

members.name: read
members.summary: Read a file's lines (eager — the whole file reads at the call).

members.name: readBytes
members.summary: Read a file's raw bytes — no decode, no line split (File.read substitutes U+FFFD and splits; this is the byte-faithful read). Bounded and in-memory: stream big data to a sink instead.

members.name: readSecret
members.summary: Read a file's whole content as a Secret (a mounted k8s/docker secret is a file); trailing newlines are trimmed.

members.name: sha256
members.summary: The SHA-256 digest of a file's bytes, lowercase hex (sha256sum parity). Streams internally — never loads the file as a value.

members.name: size
members.summary: The file's size as a Size — compare directly (File.size p > 10MiB); Size.toBytes for the int. Raises when absent (the plain name asserts; a trySize is a park).
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
let f = $"{d}/a.txt"
["x"] |> File.write f
print $"{File.size f}"
Dir.deleteAll d

members.name: stat
members.summary: The path's FileRow — ls's own row for ONE path, so `Path.glob ... |> Seq.map File.stat` turns strings into rows. Describes a symlink ITSELF (kind Symlink, target Some), not what it points at. Raises when absent — and a glob hit can vanish before stat reaches it (the glob TIMING seam).
members.example:
let d = Path.newTempDir ()
let f = $"{d}/a.txt"
["x"] |> File.write f
print (File.stat f).name
Dir.deleteAll d

members.name: write
members.summary: Write a sequence of lines to a file (overwrites).

members.name: writeBytes
members.summary: Write raw bytes to a file — the byte-faithful sink (File.write encodes lines and appends LF).

members.name: abs
members.summary: The absolute value.

members.name: average
members.summary: The mean of floats (raises on empty; finite-only).

members.name: near
members.summary: True when a and b differ by at most eps — the equality idiom (floats do not join '==').

members.name: ofInt
members.summary: An int as a float — the explicit widening (weir never widens implicitly).

members.name: parse
members.summary: Parse float text — the shape show renders (raises on anything else, including NaN/Infinity: weir floats are finite).

members.name: round
members.summary: Round to the nearest whole, halves away from zero (2.5 rounds to 3.0).

members.name: sum
members.summary: Sum floats (the sum must stay finite — the floats law). Seq.sum stays seq<int>; each numeric type owns its sum.

members.name: toInt
members.summary: The integer part, truncating toward zero (raises outside the 64-bit range).

members.name: tryParse
members.summary: Float.parse as an Option — None instead of the raise.

members.name: defaults
members.summary: The request template RECORD: method = Get, empty url, NoAuth, no body, 30s timeout. `Http.send { Http.defaults with url = u }`. Sibling that reads alike: `Http.get url` is a CONSTRUCTOR returning one of these.

members.name: delete
members.summary: Constructor: a Delete request to the url.

members.name: fetch
members.summary: The raising GET shorthand: takes a BARE URL (never a request — a built request runs through Http.send), returns body only, RAISES on non-2xx naming the status (the `curl -sf` / JS `fetch(url)` analogue). Http.fetch raises where Http.send returns — two names, no boolean.

members.name: get
members.summary: A request CONSTRUCTOR — returns an HttpRequest, makes NO request: `Http.get u` = `{ Http.defaults with method = Get; url = u }`; run it with Http.send. Add optionals with `with`: `Http.send { Http.get u with auth = Bearer t }`. The URL-in-body-out shorthand is Http.fetch.

members.name: head
members.summary: Constructor: a Head request to the url.

members.name: options
members.summary: Constructor: an Options request to the url.

members.name: patch
members.summary: Constructor: a Patch request to the url.

members.name: post
members.summary: Constructor: a Post request to the url (add body/auth with `with`).

members.name: put
members.summary: Constructor: a Put request to the url.

members.name: query
members.summary: Constructor: a QUERY request (RFC 10008) — idempotent, so `retry` around it is safe by the method's definition. Almost nothing serves it yet; expect 405.

members.name: send
members.summary: Run a request. Status is DATA (a 404 binds; only transport failure raises). A Json body carries `to json` lines byte-exact; auth is a Secret-carrying union; show masks secrets.

members.name: withQuery
members.summary: Append a percent-encoded query string to a url — params first, the url last (data-last: `url |> Http.withQuery [(k, v)]`); keys and values are escaped, so a space or `&` cannot break the url. (NOT `Http.query` the method constructor.)

members.name: epochMs
members.summary: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch, as an int — the interop escape (JSON fields, date +%s%3N).

members.name: now
members.summary: The current instant (UTC).

members.name: ofEpochMs
members.summary: The instant at an epoch-milliseconds int.

members.name: parse
members.summary: An ISO 8601 timestamp (Z or a numeric offset, normalized to UTC; a bare date reads as midnight UTC). Raises on anything else — tryParse asks.

members.name: parseWith
members.summary: Read a timestamp by a NAMED format — %Y %m %d %e (1-2 digit day) %b (Jan..Dec) %H %M %S %f %z (%% literal), other text literal. PREFIX semantics: a log line's tail rides free. No %z means UTC. Raises on mismatch, naming the position.

members.name: tryParse
members.summary: Some instant, or None when the text is not ISO 8601.

members.name: tryParseWith
members.summary: Some instant, or None when the line does not match (an unknown DIRECTIVE still raises — that is a format bug, not a data miss).

members.name: debug
members.summary: Write a DEBUG line to stderr; hidden unless WEIR_LOG=debug (or trace). Stdout is DATA — every Log member writes to stderr, a law with no stream knob.

members.name: debugWith
members.summary: Log.debug's thunk twin: the message computes ONLY when the level passes.

members.name: info
members.summary: Write an INFO line to stderr — shown by default (WEIR_LOG=level moves the threshold, case-insensitive; off silences).

members.name: infoWith
members.summary: Log.info's thunk twin: the message computes ONLY when the level passes.

members.name: trace
members.summary: Write a TRACE line to stderr — the innermost-detail level, hidden unless WEIR_LOG=trace.

members.name: traceWith
members.summary: Log.trace's thunk twin: the message computes ONLY when the level passes (weir has no lazy argument position — the Option.defaultWith precedent for the expensive argument).

members.name: warn
members.summary: Write a WARN line to stderr — the highest level, shown unless WEIR_LOG=off.

members.name: warnWith
members.summary: Log.warn's thunk twin: the message computes ONLY when the level passes.

members.name: add
members.summary: A new map with the entry set (replacing an existing key); the original is untouched.

members.name: count
members.summary: The number of entries.

members.name: get
members.summary: The value under a key (raises naming the key when absent — tryGet asks).

members.name: has
members.summary: True when a key is present.

members.name: keys
members.summary: The keys, sorted.

members.name: ofPairs
members.summary: Build a map from (key, value) pairs; duplicate keys last-win (the JSON boundary's law).

members.name: pairs
members.summary: The entries as (key, value) pairs, key-sorted.

members.name: remove
members.summary: A new map without the key (absent is fine); the original is untouched.

members.name: tryGet
members.summary: Some value when the key is present, None when not.

members.name: values
members.summary: The values, in key-sorted order.

members.name: portOpen
members.summary: True when 127.0.0.1:<port> accepts a TCP connection (250ms attempt) — poll's readiness body. Remote hosts on a receipt.

members.name: defaultValue
members.summary: The Some value, or a fallback when None.

members.name: defaultWith
members.summary: Like defaultValue, but the fallback is computed only when None.

members.name: iter
members.summary: Run a unit effect on the Some value; None runs NOTHING (a Some-only side effect with no match ceremony).

members.name: map
members.summary: Apply a function inside a Some, pass None through.

members.name: orElse
members.summary: The option itself when Some, else the FALLBACK (fallback first, so it pipes data-last). Stays in Option — Option.defaultValue is the one that UNWRAPS. The fallback is an ordinary eager argument (an orElseWith twin is parked on the defaultWith precedent).

members.name: combine
members.summary: Join two path segments.

members.name: dir
members.summary: The directory part of a path.

members.name: extension
members.summary: The extension, including the dot.

members.name: fileName
members.summary: The final component of a path.

members.name: glob
members.summary: Match a glob against the filesystem (lazy; globstar skips symlinks).

members.name: newTempDir
members.summary: CREATE a fresh unique directory under the temp root and return its path (within tmp's naming). Cleanup is the caller's or the OS's — use `within tmp dir` for removal on scope exit (which the exit hook also sweeps on Ctrl+C/kill); newTempDir DELIBERATELY outlives the block and is never swept.

members.name: stem
members.summary: The file name without its extension.

members.name: tempRoot
members.summary: The system temp directory (a pure query; no trailing separator, platform-native).

members.name: under
members.summary: The confining join: combine, normalise, then RAISE if the result escapes base — segment-wise, so uploads-evil is not under uploads. combine is for paths you control; under is for paths you do not. Purely textual (never follows symlinks or touches the disk); absolute and Windows-shaped second arguments refuse on every platform.

members.name: defaults
members.summary: The poll template: timeout = 1m, interval = 1s.

members.name: pid
members.summary: The child's OS process id.
members.pointer: within proc p = <command> binds the handle; see #help within

members.name: running
members.summary: True while the child has not exited.
members.pointer: poll watch=p checks this for you, with better errors

members.name: stop
members.summary: Tree-kill and reap now, idempotent; the scope's exit is then a no-op.

members.name: tail
members.summary: The child's last ~100 output lines (stderr first) from the spill — readable while it runs.

members.name: wait
members.summary: Block until the child exits NATURALLY; its exit code as data. The way to let a scoped process finish — the scope's own exit kills.

members.name: defaults
members.summary: The retry template: attempts = 5, delay = 1s, timeout = None. `retry attempts=5` is `retry { Retry.defaults with attempts = 5 }`.

members.name: map
members.summary: Transform a secret's value, keeping it secret. `Secret.map (fun t -> "Bearer " + t)` stays secret where reveal-then-concat would not.

members.name: of
members.summary: ASSERT that a string is secret — the SAFE direction, for computed secrets (a generated token, a derived key). show renders ***; Secret.reveal is the one exit.

members.name: reveal
members.summary: The one guarded exit: the secret's plain value. Every use of the value (a header, a hash) is a deliberate reveal — the audit is the call site.

members.name: append
members.summary: Concatenate two sequences, lazily.

members.name: average
members.summary: The mean of ints AS A FLOAT (raises on empty — absence is Option's job). Float/Size/Duration own their means (Float.average …).

members.name: choose
members.summary: Map and drop the None results in one lazy pass.
members.example: [1; 2; 3] |> Seq.choose (fun x -> if x > 1 then Some x else None) |> Seq.force

members.name: chunkBySize
members.summary: Split into consecutive chunks of at most n, lazily — the batching member (the last chunk may be short).

members.name: collect
members.summary: Map each element to a sequence and flatten, lazily (F#'s collect; flatMap elsewhere).

members.name: concat
members.summary: Flatten a sequence of sequences, lazily (collect with the identity).

members.name: contains
members.summary: True when an element is present.

members.name: countBy
members.summary: Count elements per projected key as (key, count) pairs, first-seen key order; forces on the first pull.

members.name: distinct
members.summary: Drop duplicate elements, keeping first order.

members.name: distinctBy
members.summary: Keep the first element per projected key, lazily — distinct's projection twin.

members.name: exactlyOne
members.summary: The one element — a cardinality ASSERTION: raises on none AND on more (head silently accepts a second element, hiding a wrong-arity source). The spelling for command output expected to be one line.

members.name: except
members.summary: Set difference: the source without the excluded values (exclusions first, source last; the exclusion set materializes on the first pull, the source streams).

members.name: exists
members.summary: True when any element satisfies a predicate.

members.name: find
members.summary: The first element a predicate accepts (raises when none match — tryFind asks).

members.name: fold
members.summary: Left-fold: thread an accumulator through the elements.

members.name: forall
members.summary: True when every element satisfies a predicate.

members.name: force
members.summary: Materialize a lazy sequence, caching it.
members.pointer: force once, then reuse freely — it memoizes (the two customers: reuse and timing).

members.name: groupBy
members.summary: Group elements by a key into Group records.

members.name: head
members.summary: The first element (raises on empty).

members.name: indexed
members.summary: Pair every element with its zero-based position, lazily — mapi/iteri are `indexed |> map`/`iter` over the tuple.

members.name: isEmpty
members.summary: True when the sequence has no elements.

members.name: item
members.summary: The element at a zero-based index (raises out of range).

members.name: iter
members.summary: Run a unit-returning effect over each element.

members.name: last
members.summary: The last element — ASSERTS the source is non-empty (the X/tryX rule; raises 'last: empty sequence'), and FORCES the whole source by necessity: an infinite source does not return.

members.name: length
members.summary: Count the elements (forces the sequence).

members.name: map
members.summary: Apply a function to every element, lazily.

members.name: max
members.summary: The largest element (Ord; raises on empty). One pass — no sort.

members.name: maxBy
members.summary: The element whose projected key is largest (Ord on the key; raises on empty).

members.name: min
members.summary: The smallest element (Ord; raises on empty). One pass — no sort.

members.name: minBy
members.summary: The element whose projected key is smallest (Ord on the key; raises on empty).

members.name: pairwise
members.summary: Adjacent pairs: (e0,e1), (e1,e2), and so on.

members.name: pfirst
members.summary: Race an arm over every element; the FIRST SUCCESS wins. Losers' spawned processes are tree-killed and their failures never surface. All arms failed rethrows the first error by input order; an empty sequence raises. A losing arm's failure is DISCARDED — if only one arm can succeed, the others' errors are hidden, so a misconfigured fan-out still looks healthy.
members.pointer: a race, not a retry: same fetch against N mirrors, first answer wins.

members.name: pfirstWith
members.summary: Seq.pfirst at an explicit concurrency ceiling.

members.name: pick
members.summary: The first Some a chooser yields (raises when none — tryPick asks).

members.name: piter
members.summary: Run an effect over each element in parallel.
members.pointer: workers fork the session (worker-local cd, dies at join).

members.name: piterWith
members.summary: Seq.piter with an explicit worker count.
members.pointer: an explicit n is never reduced by nesting; piter's default ladder is.

members.name: pmap
members.summary: Map in parallel across worker threads.
members.pointer: ordered, eager, at most 64 workers; the first error by input order wins.

members.name: pmapWith
members.summary: Seq.pmap with an explicit worker count — the sizing knob for rate-limited or memory-heavy arms.
members.pointer: an explicit n is never reduced by nesting; pmap's default ladder is.

members.name: range
members.summary: A lazy arithmetic range: start, step, stop.

members.name: reduce
members.summary: Fold without a seed: the first element starts the accumulator (raises on empty — fold takes the seed).

members.name: replicate
members.summary: n copies of one value, lazily (raises on a negative count).

members.name: rev
members.summary: Reverse. FORCES the whole input on the first pull (never an infinite seq).

members.name: scan
members.summary: Fold emitting every intermediate state, the seed first, lazily.

members.name: skip
members.summary: Drop the first n elements, keep the rest lazily.

members.name: skipWhile
members.summary: Drop the leading run the predicate accepts, lazily; the rest streams whole.

members.name: sort
members.summary: Sort ascending by the elements themselves (Ord); forces on the first pull.

members.name: sortBy
members.summary: Order by a key projection.

members.name: sortByDescending
members.summary: Order by a key projection, descending.

members.name: sortDescending
members.summary: Sort descending by the elements themselves (Ord); forces on the first pull.

members.name: sum
members.summary: Add the elements of an int sequence.

members.name: take
members.summary: The first n elements, lazily; pairs with Seq.skip.

members.name: takeWhile
members.summary: Elements while the predicate holds, lazily; stops at the first refusal.

members.name: tryExactlyOne
members.summary: exactlyOne's Option twin: Some when the sequence has exactly one element, None on none or more.

members.name: tryFind
members.summary: The first element a predicate accepts, as an Option.

members.name: tryHead
members.summary: The first element as an Option, None when empty.

members.name: tryItem
members.summary: The element at an index as an Option.

members.name: tryLast
members.summary: The last element as an Option (None when empty) — the asking twin; forces the whole source.

members.name: tryPick
members.summary: The first Some a chooser yields, as an Option — choose-then-head in one pass.

members.name: where
members.summary: Keep the elements a predicate accepts, lazily.

members.name: windowed
members.summary: Sliding windows of size n, LAZY (produced as the source is pulled; a short source yields the EMPTY seq — no partial window; windows view the same memoized elements). Raises when n <= 0.

members.name: zip
members.summary: Pair two sequences element-wise, stopping at the shorter.

members.name: average
members.summary: The mean size, truncated to whole bytes (raises on empty).

members.name: bytes
members.summary: A size of n bytes — the literal 512B, as a function.

members.name: parse
members.summary: Parse size text: binary units at 1024 (1.5MiB), the SI spellings at powers of ten (1MB is 10^6 — the writer chose the unit), B for bytes; sub-byte precision raises.

members.name: sum
members.summary: Sum sizes — total bytes as a Size.

members.name: toBytes
members.summary: The total bytes as an int — the exact exit (show's rendering truncates to one decimal).

members.name: tryParse
members.summary: Size.parse as an Option — None instead of the raise.

members.name: contains
members.summary: True when a substring is present.

members.name: endsWith
members.summary: True when the string ends with a suffix.

members.name: fromBase64
members.summary: Decode standard base64 (padded or unpadded) to text; raises on invalid input OR when the bytes are not valid UTF-8 (never U+FFFD corruption).

members.name: fromUtf8
members.summary: Decode Bytes as text; raises when the bytes are not valid UTF-8 OR contain NUL (the encoding law's gate — corruption never wears a success).

members.name: isMatch
members.summary: True when a regex matches anywhere in the string.

members.name: join
members.summary: Join a sequence of strings with a separator.

members.name: length
members.summary: The number of characters.

members.name: replace
members.summary: Replace every occurrence of a substring.

members.name: rmatch
members.summary: The first regex match's groups as an Option of a sequence (positional groups; named `(?<x>...)` rejects — weir names captures at the binder).

members.name: rmatchAll
members.summary: Every regex match's groups, as a sequence of sequences.

members.name: sha256
members.summary: The SHA-256 digest of the string's UTF-8 bytes, lowercase hex (sha256sum parity). sha256 only — more algorithms on receipt.

members.name: split
members.summary: Split on a separator into a sequence.

members.name: splitOnce
members.summary: Split at the FIRST occurrence into (before, after) — the tail stays intact, separators and all; raises when the separator is absent (trySplitOnce is the Option twin).

members.name: startsWith
members.summary: True when the string starts with a prefix.

members.name: sub
members.summary: A substring by start index and length.

members.name: toBase64
members.summary: Base64 of the string's UTF-8 bytes — ONE unwrapped line (no 76-column MIME wrap, no -w0 tax).

members.name: toInt
members.summary: Parse an int (raises on a non-number).

members.name: toLower
members.summary: Lowercase (invariant culture).

members.name: toUpper
members.summary: Uppercase (invariant culture).

members.name: toUtf8
members.summary: The string's UTF-8 bytes as a Bytes value.

members.name: trim
members.summary: Drop leading and trailing whitespace.

members.name: trimEnd
members.summary: Drop trailing whitespace.

members.name: trimStart
members.summary: Drop leading whitespace.

members.name: tryFromBase64
members.summary: fromBase64 as an Option: None for malformed base64 and for valid-base64-of-non-text alike.

members.name: tryFromUtf8
members.summary: fromUtf8 as an Option: None for non-text bytes, NUL included.

members.name: tryIndexOf
members.summary: The index of a substring as an Option.

members.name: trySplitOnce
members.summary: splitOnce's Option twin: Some (before, after) at the first occurrence, None when the separator is absent — the KEY=VALUE parser's shape.
members.example: match Str.trySplitOnce "=" "key=val" with | Some (k, v) -> print k | None -> print "no"

members.name: tryToInt
members.summary: Parse an int as an Option, None when it is not a number.

forms.name: Completed
forms.summary: A finished command: exitCode, stdout, stderr. You get one from `| complete`.

forms.name: EnvVar
forms.summary: A name/value environment pair. From `Env.vars` / `pair` / `ofPairs` / `fromFile`.

forms.name: FileRow
forms.summary: A directory entry: name, kind (Regular | Directory | Symlink — a fact, not an answer), target (Some for a symlink, None otherwise — the one fact no File.* query answers), bytes (0 B for a directory), modified (the last-write Instant — the file's own fact, stable under binding; the table renders it relatively, show keeps ISO), hidden, path. From `ls` — files AND subdirectories, SORTED by name (ordinal: case-sensitive, uppercase first; never the locale). name is for MATCHING and display; path is for handing to File.* - name derives from path, never the reverse. Narrow facts are queries, not columns: File.mode for permissions.

forms.name: Group
forms.summary: A key and its items, from `Seq.groupBy`.

forms.name: cd
forms.summary: Change the session's directory, returning the OLD one (restore by binding: `let prev = cd "/tmp"`). A bare name applies a BINDING (`cd target`); `~` expands; `within cd` is the scoped spelling.

forms.name: complete
forms.summary: Reify a command chain to a Completed record (exitCode, stdout, stderr).
forms.pointer: the reifier law: output goes where the meaning goes.

forms.name: exit
forms.summary: Exit the process with a status code.

forms.name: exitCode
forms.summary: Reify a command to its integer exit code.
forms.pointer: the reifier law: the meaning is the code.

forms.name: fail
forms.summary: Stop with a message and exit code 1.
forms.pointer: message-carrying; `exit n` is the bare-code spelling.

forms.name: force
forms.summary: Materialize a lazy sequence, caching it (the bare Seq.force).

forms.name: from json
forms.summary: Parse ONE JSON document (any number of lines — a pretty-printed HTTP body pipes straight in) into a declared record. Fields are int/string/bool/float or Option of one; an Option field reads a missing key or null as None.
forms.pointer: a pipe stage: resp.body |> from json Config.

forms.name: from jsonl
forms.summary: Parse a JSON line stream — one document per element (NDJSON, the shape `to jsonl` writes) — into declared records.
forms.pointer: a pipe stage: xs |> from jsonl Config.

forms.name: from yaml
forms.summary: Parse YAML lines (the strict subset: block maps/sequences, scalars, # comments; --- multi-doc) into a declared record TREE — nested records, seqs, seq<string * _> mappings, Option (missing/null reads None). Anchors, tags, and flow style are rejected.
forms.pointer: a pipe stage: lines |> from yaml Deployment — yields seq<Deployment>, one per document.

forms.name: not
forms.summary: Boolean negation.

forms.name: orFail
forms.summary: Stream a command's output, raising with a message on a nonzero exit.
forms.pointer: the reifier law: output streams, the exit is the meaning.

forms.name: poll
forms.summary: retry's time-bounded twin: `poll timeout=5m interval=10s` + a readiness body. `watch=<proc>` fails FAST when the scoped process dies (its last output rides the error) and stamps the watched state on a timeout.
forms.pointer: the wait-for-ready shape: within proc srv = … then poll timeout=10s watch=srv + Net.portOpen <port>

forms.name: print
forms.summary: Write a value and a trailing newline to stdout.

forms.name: printerr
forms.summary: Write a value and a newline to stderr.

forms.name: retry
forms.summary: Re-run a body until its predicate passes: `retry attempts=5 delay=30s` + an indented body. A bool body IS the predicate; a value body takes `until r` + a predicate block and yields the value. Exhaustion raises; raises inside the body propagate (make failure data with | succeeds / | complete).
forms.pointer: options are a record underneath: retry { Retry.defaults with attempts = 3 }

forms.name: show
forms.summary: Render a value to its string form — the SAME text an interpolation hole gives. Reach for it where a hole cannot go: point-free positions (Seq.map show) and Secrets (masked). Total; functions show opaquely.

forms.name: succeeds
forms.summary: Reify a command to a bool: did it exit zero?
forms.pointer: the reifier law: the meaning is the verdict.

forms.name: to json
forms.summary: Render ONE value as ONE JSON document (minified, one line): a record is an object, a seq an array (forced — one line cannot stream). A None field omits its key (so from json reads it back as None).
forms.pointer: a pipe stage: payload |> to json.

forms.name: to jsonl
forms.summary: Render a sequence to JSON lines — one document per element (NDJSON, the shape `from jsonl` reads), lazily.
forms.pointer: a pipe stage: xs |> to jsonl.

forms.name: to yaml
forms.summary: Render a value tree (records, seqs, scalars, Option, Yaml nodes) to YAML lines. A seq renders ---separated documents; a None field omits its key; strings that could be mis-typed (no, 007, 1e5) are quoted.
forms.pointer: a pipe stage: deployment |> to yaml.

forms.name: within
forms.summary: A scoped resource for an indented block, released on EVERY exit (normal and raise): `tmp` — a fresh directory, removed when the block exits; `cd` — the working directory for the block, restored after; `env` — an environment overlay for the block's children; `proc` — a background process, tree-killed and reaped when the block exits; `lock` — an advisory file lock, held for the block, released on every exit (kill -9 included).
forms.pointer: within proc srv = <command> binds a Proc handle; the tree is killed and reaped at scope exit
